title: Adaptive retention & ephemeral buffering for VPC/on‑prem collectors
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Private and Dedicated customers run isolated collectors with intermittent egress to Redwood control plane or Kafka bridges. We currently apply coarse global sampling and retention which either over-retains tenant data (cost & compliance risk) or drops too aggressively (loss of signal). We need per-tenant adaptive retention profiles and ephemeral local buffering that: (1) respect per-tenant legal/retention policies, (2) preserve high‑priority traces/metrics during transient network partitions, and (3) limit on-device storage with encrypted disk and tenant QoS isolation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Collector config supports per-tenant retention_profile and sampling_profile fields and can be hot-reloaded from control plane. 2) Local buffer implemented with configurable max_size_mb, encrypted on disk (KMS integration), and evicts using per-tenant LRU policies when full. 3) During simulated egress outage (10m/30m), high-priority traces (priority>=90) are preserved and flushed on reconnect. 4) Metrics and Prometheus instrumentation added: buffer_used_bytes, buffer_evictions_total{tenant}, flush_success_total, retention_enforced_total{tenant}. 5) End-to-end test: deploy private collector in CI environment, run tenant traffic at 200 rps, simulate egress loss and validate retention rules applied and buffered items flushed after recovery. 6) Documentation: Confluence config guide and migration notes; upgrade path for existing private customers.
technical_notes: Implementation plan: - Extend collector config schema: retention_profiles: list of {name, min_ttl_days, max_ttl_days, legal_hold_flag, priority_threshold, storage_quota_mb}. sampling_profiles: {rate, algorithm, dynamic_boost_rules}. - Buffer: write append-only LZ4 chunk files under $COLLECTOR_DATA/buffer/, encryption via envelope keys from KMS (support AWS KMS and HSM tokens). Chunk metadata contains tenant_id, sequence, priority histogram. - Eviction: tenant-aware LRU with quota enforcement. Overflow eviction triggers metrics and optional customer-facing telemetry event. - Hot-reload: control plane exposes /v1/collector-config and signed config blobs; collectors validate signatures. - Sharding: consistent hashing on tenant_id for multi-collector fleets; on reconnect, collectors reconcile outstanding sequence IDs with bridge. - Backpressure: when buffer > 80% global quota, advertise backpressure via gRPC/HTTP 429 with Retry-After and increment buffer_backpressure_total. - Tests: unit coverage for retention enforcement, integration for KMS envelope encryption mock, chaos tests for network partition and reconnect flush. - Rollout: feature flag controlled via control plane; default conservative retention for existing installs.
progress_updates: 2025-03-11: Spike complete — validated LZ4 chunking approach and envelope encryption with AWS KMS (POC in collector branch). PR: github.com/redwood/collector/pull/1422 (POC, do not merge).

2025-03-13: Schema proposal reviewed with Product and Security. Added legal_hold_flag to retention profile. Feedback: require signed config blobs over TLS + HMAC. Action: add signature verification step to hot-reload flow.
2025-03-15: Implemented buffer metrics and eviction counter; added tenant tag to evictions. Local tests show eviction fairness across tenants with synthetic load.
decisions: Store buffer chunks on-disk encrypted using envelope encryption (KMS) rather than only in-memory to survive collector restarts.
Eviction policy: per-tenant soft quota + global hard cap. Soft quota triggers increased sampling for affected tenant (dynamic_boost_rules).
Signed config blobs served from control plane will be required for hot-reload to prevent config spoofing in private installs.
